subject: Bull Market Anniversary For The S&P 500

 Click here to take the poll and don't forget to share your thoughts in the WSB comments section . 
 
 
 
 
 
    
 
 
 
    
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 King Khalid: Saudi Arabia's main airport rocked by back-to-back Houthi attacks .

 Who is Decart? From AI startup to Amazon's ( AMZN ) $7B acquisition target .

 'Another con': J.P. Morgan questions credibility of Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire .


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Big milestone 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 More than double your money in four years. That's not a bad investment, and in fact, it trounces many returns, especially when it's an overall index and not a stock on a rip.

The benchmark in reference is none other than the S&P 500 ( SP500 ), which is celebrating its fourth bull market anniversary today. Back on Oct. 12, 2022, the index hit its final bear-market closing low of 3,577, and only a few years later, those digits have spun ahead to 7,811, marking a gain of nearly 120%.

Helping to achieve this massive return have been several catalysts. Consumer spending and labor markets remained extraordinarily resilient despite years of inflation and interest rate hikes. Investors have also been willing to pay higher premiums for future earnings, which have been strong and led the S&P 500 to record massive double-digit earnings growth. Last, but not least, has been the AI revolution, boosting everything from semiconductors and hyperscalers to power grids and utilities.

 Market breadth? "Technology distribution is now truly global, a handful of companies have aggregated demand on top of it, and with near-zero marginal cost, much of every incremental dollar of revenue falls straight to the bottom line. Concentrated market cap hence looks more like the market faithfully mirroring where the profits have actually gone," SA analyst MBI Deep Dives wrote in S&P 500 Index Concentration - Room At The Top . "Current market breadth deterioration is attributed to higher interest rates, not fears of slowing economic growth, reducing the severity of the signal," Hugo Ferrer added in Why The Negative Market Breadth Is Not A Negative Factor This Time .

 Free Webinar: The Next Stage of the AI Boom 
 
 
 
 
 
 Billions continue to pour into chips, data centers, and AI infrastructure. But as the financing behind that investment grows more complex, questions are emerging about how sustainable the current pace may be.

 Join Steven Cress, VP of Quantitative Strategy, and Kevin M. Sanford, Quantitative Macro Strategist, as they examine the forces driving the AI boom, the risks emerging beneath the surface, and parallels with the late-1990s dot-com era .

 They’ll also take a closer look at Nvidia’s position at the center of AI spending and what its valuation may be signaling about investor expectations for the next stage of AI growth.
